solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Moral principles in one county somewhat lispingly mentioned?

indicators.note: spoken with a lisp, each S comes out as TH, so the county name said this way gives the sound we want

parts.note: Essex is an English county east of London

explanation.surface: A question about the moral code of some English county, delivered with an odd speech impediment.
explanation.walkthrough: Say ESSEX with a lisp and the S sounds turn to TH: 'Eth-ix'. 'somewhat lispingly mentioned' signals the sound-alike, and 'somewhat' excuses the inexact match.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person's code of right and wrong conduct is their set of moral principles.

clue.text: Tentacle finally flung out to swallow up

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Tentacle
out signals that the letters of flung are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: An octopus or squid flings out a tentacle to grab and swallow its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from Tentacle; 'out' rearranges FLUNG to NGULF.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to engulf is to overwhelm or envelop completely, as a wave might swallow up a boat.

clue.text: All gathered for this dinner?

parts.note: reads as guests assembling for a meal, but 'gathered' also means crops brought in, and the feast celebrates the end of bringing them in

explanation.surface: Everyone has assembled for a dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' means both assembled (of people) and brought in (of crops); the meal marks the completion of the gathering of the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a traditional church or village meal held to celebrate bringing in the year's crops.

clue.text: Credit cinema employee, one doing the grind

parts.note: CR is the standard accounting abbreviation for credit
an usher shows people to their seats in a cinema

explanation.surface: A cinema worker hailed as someone who toils away at the daily grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: a machine or person that crushes or grinds things down, as a stone mill does.

clue.text: Compulsory for daughter to tour church

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so these letters go around the church abbreviation

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Is it obligatory for a daughter to go round a church on a visit?
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is not a link word here: it supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something forced is imposed and not voluntary, just as compulsory things are.

clue.text: Order, "Time up" — it's the end

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for Time is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A referee calls time, and the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The online text 'After round' gives no M; the printed 'Order' gives OM (Order of Merit). 'up' reverses AGE to EGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so figuratively the conclusion of anything.

clue.text: France, say, puts up large residences

parts.note: France is an example of a nation; 'say' marks it as an example
to put someone up is to give them lodging, which is to house them

explanation.surface: France provides lodgings for guests in some grand homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: big homes standing on rural estates are the classic stately residences of the gentry.

clue.text: Very fond of acting, securing opening in theatre

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the word for acting holds the letter inside it

parts.note: doing is acting, as in 'what are you doing?'

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from theatre

explanation.surface: Someone adores the stage, having landed a first role in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts T, the first letter of theatre, inside DOING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being doting means showing excessive, adoring affection, so very fond of someone.

clue.text: Within reason, love to circulate

indicators.note: within says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a ground is a reason, as in grounds for complaint
love is nil in tennis, written as the O shape of zero

explanation.surface: Spreading love, within reason, among people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within' puts O into GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that goes round passes from person to person, as a rumour or bottle circulates.

clue.text: Girl, less bubbly, may acquire spirits from here?

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
a still drink has no fizz, so a less bubbly one is stiller

explanation.surface: A flat, rather unlively girl who might obtain spirits, as if from a medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests ghosts but means strong drink; the definition is cryptic because the maker is where the liquor comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a producer of whisky, gin and other strong drink is where such liquor is bought from.

clue.text: Go up in game in record time

indicators.note: in says the game abbreviation sits inside the record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone climbs the rankings in a game in record-breaking time.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; the second is the containment signal. An EP is an extended-play record.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to erupt is to burst out upwards, as a volcano blows its top.

clue.text: In shelter, check what may have drawn blood

parts.note: a lee is a sheltered side, out of the wind
CH is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: Someone examining an injury in a shelter after a wounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn blood' suggests a wound; it is the bloodsucking worm once used by doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this bloodsucking worm was applied by old physicians to draw blood from patients.

clue.text: In nursing-home, somewhat bleak

indicators.note: In says the word for somewhat is placed inside the home

parts.note: a san, short for sanatorium, is a place for nursing invalids
part means somewhat, as in 'part true'

explanation.surface: A care home is described as rather grim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' looks like a containment signal, but the whole of 'nursing-home' is the sanatorium abbreviation; 'In' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: austere and lacking comfort, after the famously frugal people of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: Make mistake with it in Conservative area

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the Conservative

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Getting something wrong in a Conservative constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a territory is a region or tract of land, an area under someone's control.

clue.text: Couplet rewritten in eight parts

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters of the word are set down again in another order

explanation.surface: A two-line verse expanded into a piece with eight sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: eightfold, made up of eight parts, as double is made of two.

clue.text: Mushroom in pack brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A fungus has turned up in a backpack someone brought along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses PACK to KCAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a kind of fungus whose cap dissolves into a black inky liquid.

clue.text: Small creature in group catches cold

indicators.note: catches means holds, so the group holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a set is a group, as of people or things
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: A small animal in a herd comes down with a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' puts C inside SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bug, beetle or fly is a small six-legged creature.

clue.text: Not involved in university, somehow learnt outside

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go around the university letter
somehow implies some unspecified rearrangement of the letters of learnt

explanation.surface: A student who stays aloof at college, picking up knowledge from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns LEARNT into NETRAL; 'outside' wraps it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a neutral party takes no side and is uninvolved in a dispute.

clue.text: Travel round grand, extensive hill-top

indicators.note: round means going around, so the travel word encloses the letter

parts.note: to ride is to travel, on a horse or bike
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A journey around a grand, sprawling summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts G inside RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a long, narrow raised crest along the top of hills is a stretched-out summit.

clue.text: Sharp point in old letter

definitions.meaning: a prickle on a rose stem
the Old English runic letter for the TH sound, still used in Icelandic

explanation.surface: A sharp remark found in an ancient piece of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the spike on a bramble, and the Anglo-Saxon character for the TH sound.

clue.text: Boy with bow and arrow in revolt, arrested by detectives

indicators.note: arrested by means held by the police, so the detectives enclose the letters

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives
up means in revolt, as in 'up in arms'

explanation.surface: An armed lad caught by police officers during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolt' gives UP as in 'up in arms'; CID is the Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the Roman god of love is shown as a winged boy with a bow and arrows.

clue.text: In organised sortie, quiet return thrust

indicators.note: In says the quiet letter is put inside the rearranged sortie
organised means put into order, so the letters of sortie are rearranged

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A military raid organised so that troops quietly hit back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' turns SORTIE into RIOSTE; 'In' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing term: a quick counter-attack made after parrying, also used for a sharp retort.

clue.text: Tight-lipped naval officer?

parts.note: looks like a secretive sailor, but one who draws the lips together tightly is one who purses them, and a ship's paymaster also has that title

explanation.surface: A discreet officer in the navy who keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight-lipped' suggests secrecy; the joke is the literal sense of lips drawn tight, puckered like a drawstring bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: the ship's officer in charge of accounts shares a name with someone who puckers their mouth.

clue.text: But these well-heeled travellers are not all black

definitions.text: But these well-heeled travellers are not all black

parts.words: But these well-heeled travellers are not all black
parts.note: jet is a black stone and a set is a group, so a group of jet would seem to be black; but the phrase means rich people who fly about the world

explanation.surface: A remark about a group of wealthy travellers and their varied complexions or clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black' points to jet, the black gemstone; the joke is that this group of fashionable fliers is named for aircraft, not colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: wealthy fashionable people who fly from one glamorous resort to another.
